title: A body poked into a lattice medium field's coupled cell reads Submerged, and flips back the moment it leaves
binding: The positive leg boots a minimal fixture whose one lattice row carries the medium facet (a filled 5-unit-deep pool) and a medium-hold-kit body spawned dry above it. world.contacts 1 reads submerged=false before any tick runs; body.pose teleports the body down into the pool and, after a short settle, world.contacts 1 reads submerged=true; body.pose then teleports it back out and, before buoyancy has time to pull it back under, world.contacts 1 reads submerged=false again — the flag genuinely flips both ways off the population's per-tick WorldFieldLattice.MediumSurface sample, not a one-shot boot fact. The discriminating leg runs the IDENTICAL script against the SAME fixture with the medium row's initial value authored 0 instead of 1 (an empty, still-declared pool) — the coupled cell never carries a positive medium value, so MediumSurface never resolves and the body reads submerged=false at every occurrence; the positive leg's submerged=true assertion never matches this transcript.

expect.name: dry-before-any-tick
expect.text: [world.contacts: p1 grounded=true planarSpeed=0.00 resolved=0 submerged=false atSurface=false obstruction=none]

expect.name: dry-again-after-posing-back-out
expect.text: [world.contacts: p1 grounded=false planarSpeed=0.00 resolved=0 submerged=false atSurface=false obstruction=none]

expect.name: reads-submerged-false-throughout
expect.text: [world.contacts: p1 grounded=false planarSpeed=0.00 resolved=0 submerged=false atSurface=false obstruction=none]
